$comment: Machine-readable registry of APR test suites and spec-requirement coverage. Verified by scripts/check-test-registry.py, which fails if a referenced fixture or test no longer exists, or if a requirement has no entry. The registry is a claim about coverage; the verifier is what makes the claim checkable. Its v1 requirements remain historical beta.3 coverage while beta.6 migration coverage is added separately.

activeMigrationTarget.coverageStatus: gated; paired representations and streams, semantic digests/manifests, CMS and unsupported proofs, fields scope, witness chains, changed forms, malformed representations, and shipped beta.6 examples are covered

gateStrength.gated: A test fails in CI if the rule is violated. The only level that actually holds an implementation.
gateStrength.partial: Some aspect of the rule is gated; other aspects are not.
gateStrength.indirect: Covered only through another component, not at this rule's own level.
gateStrength.external: Gated by a third-party suite this project does not maintain.
gateStrength.none: No test would fail if the rule were broken.
gateStrength.informative: Not a testable rule — definitional or explanatory text.

dimensions.completeness: Does the component do everything it claims?
dimensions.conformance: Does it agree with the format? (corpus + schema gates)
dimensions.correctness: Does it give right answers? (unit tests + coverage gate)
dimensions.robustness: Does it survive bad input and stay fixed? (edge cases, fuzz, mutation, regression)

suites.gate: schema agrees with every corpus fixture
suites.notes: Deliberately uses no .NET, so it fails the way a third-party SDK would.

suites.gate: ratcheting coverage (a floor, not a bar)
suites.robustnessNotes: CliRobustnessTests points empty, truncated, non-JSON, UTF-16, 50k-nested, binary and wrong-shape files at validate/info/stats. Contract: non-zero exit, no throw, no stack trace in output. Found that `info` exited 0 on any JSON object at all.

suites.notes: GUI suite runs (issue #30 fixed). Conformance is direct rather than inherited, and the project is now inside a coverage gate for the first time - it was excluded entirely while its GUI tests could not run, so there was nothing meaningful to measure. No tests are skipped anywhere in the solution.
AT-SPI smoke test is manual, outside CI. No tests are skipped anywhere in the solution.
The only third-party conformance check in the project.

suites.gate: every shipped beta.6 example must satisfy the published schema and beta.6 parser gate
suites.notes: All 19 real form files - SF-86, IRS 990, IRS 1040, W-4, the bundled starter templates and two importer outputs. Enumerated from disk, so a new file is covered without being listed anywhere. The conformance corpus is synthetic by design, one rule per fixture; these catch what only shows up at the size and messiness of a real form. Found a shipped example that failed our own validator, and the editor bug that produced it.

suites.gate: processability findings, form-vs-template comparison, and the CLI exit-code contract (0 process / 2 route to a human / 1 unreadable)
suites.notes: Implements specification 6.2 warnings as a receiver-facing report, plus a comparison against the claimed template. Covers the case no response-level check can: a prompt keeping its id while its label changes, so a pipeline files a truthful answer under a question nobody asked.

suites.gate: each workflow the GUI supports, carried start to finish through real files on disk and reloaded to check what was actually written
suites.notes: The suite had deep per-command coverage and a driver that activates every control, but nothing carried a task from beginning to end. These author a template, fill one, edit a saved form, build and fill a table, undo/redo a whole session, fill one party’s share of a multi-party form, walk the wizard, and export a fillable PDF. Partial on completeness: signing and PDF import journeys are still covered only per command.

suites.gate: the shared conformance corpus plus APR CEL binding tests in a locked uv environment
suites.notes: Locked with uv and corpus-gated. Evaluates APR CEL bindings; signatures remain opaque and unchecked.

suites.gate: npm ci && npm test: valid, invalid, malformed, unknown-member, expression-preservation, signature-preservation, and exact-response corpus coverage
suites.notes: Evaluates APR CEL bindings for numeric, boolean, string, list, and dynamic date/time values; signatures remain preserved but unchecked.

suites.gate: npm ci && npm test: semantic order, widget mapping, escaping, accessible help, unknown-type fallback, bidi isolation, and no-network rendering
suites.notes: The renderer is an optional host package, not part of the format-only core. Browser-extension tests are added when that product exists.

suites.gate: npm ci && npm test: local load, safe render, response update, and APRF download workflow
suites.notes: The demo is intentionally local-only: it does not upload a document or follow submission URLs.

suites.gate: the shared valid, invalid, and malformed corpus under Java 21
suites.notes: Project-local Maven wrapper resolves official CEL-Java. Expressions are evaluated; signatures remain preserved but unchecked.

testKinds.notes: veraPDF for PDF/A; cel-spec's suite available for the expression language now that CEL is adopted.

In-process automation-tree assertions run headlessly (AutomationTreeTests). External AT-SPI verification against a live application is still the manual script at tests/at-spi/run_at_spi_smoke.sh, outside CI. Two stubs that claimed to cover this were removed rather than left permanently skipped - a skip hides a gap instead of recording it.
Stryker.NET reports Killed:0. Until it runs, line coverage remains an incomplete behavior-quality signal.

Deterministic mutation fuzzing of the parser (ParserFuzzTests): every truncation and 200 seeded single-character corruptions per corpus fixture, plus hand-built exhaustion structures. Fixed seed so a failure reproduces. Not coverage-guided - a real fuzzer (SharpFuzz) would explore further.
Vision targets 1000+ prompts under 1s; largest fixture is 20.
Requires two conformant implementations; only one exists.

requirements.statement: BCP 14 keywords are normative only in all capitals
Presentation trivia carries no meaning; everything else round-trips
Each processing role carries the stated obligations
requirements.gap: Role obligations are gated individually by the entries below; no single vector asserts the role table itself.

requirements.statement: Presentation, serialization, model, and assertion failures are distinguishable
version MUST be 1.0-beta.6; retired embedded signatures are reported
A form is an object of version, documentType, metadata, sections, roles
Root member requiredness, domains, and defaults
metadata.title required non-blank; filledForm declares templateId
Section requires id and title and at least one prompt or child section
Prompt requires id and label; label is the accessible name
Every defined hint member, and the expectedDataType registry
requirements.gap: No beta.6 fixture exercises an unregistered expectedDataType degrading to text.

requirements.statement: Constraints JSON Schema cannot express that a validator MUST enforce
requirements.gap: Id uniqueness is gated. Ragged-table-is-advisory has no beta.6 vector.

requirements.statement: A response is always a JSON string; null coerces on read, never on write
requirements.gap: No beta.6 malformed fixture carries a non-string response.

requirements.statement: No hint rejects, alters, or blocks a response
requirements.gap: Advisory behavior is gated in client tests; no beta.6 corpus vector asserts it.

requirements.statement: kind=table is a structural claim licensing no layout data
requirements.gap: No beta.6 corpus fixture carries a table section.

requirements.statement: Unknown members round-trip and enter whole-document digests
Opening a form or attestation contacts no network location
Semantic order, labels as accessible names, complete keyboard operation
JSONC and YAML spellings carry one semantic model; UTF-8 encoding
JSONC adds comments and trailing commas; duplicate keys are rejected
Restricted YAML: string keys, safe loader, forbidden constructs rejected
requirements.gap: Only anchors have a vector. Tags, merge keys, non-finite numbers, binary, implicit dates and constructors are unexercised.

requirements.statement: Independent records, no dedup, no positional selection, RFC 7464 framing
requirements.gap: Mixed-representation stream rejection has no fixture.

requirements.statement: Paired JSONC and YAML streams yield the same semantic records
jcs-sha256 over the semantic model; manifests hold no plaintext
Attestation record members, requiredness, and closed sub-objects
Proofs cover the proof-free envelope; unsupported types are unverifiable
valid, invalid, unresolved, unverifiable, witnessed; status never gates data
Unknown members, data types, roles, and proof types degrade rather than reject
Exact-match version rejection; no MAJOR.MINOR negotiation
Parsing terminates; at least 16 levels of section nesting supported
No registered media type; representation determined by content, not name
requirements.gap: documentType-over-extension has no beta.6 fixture; the beta.3 vector was removed with its corpus.

requirements.statement: Structural checks that decide whether a document is a valid APR document
Well-formed UTF-8, no NUL or unpaired surrogates, restricted control characters
A document is never invalid because of what a response means
Advisory feedback never blocks saving, input, or declares a document invalid
requirements.gap: Client behaviour is gated in desktop tests; no corpus vector asserts the never-blocks rule.

requirements.statement: expectedDataType is an affordance; it never constrains a response, and degrades to text
Expressions are pure, never authoritative over a response, and fail data-preservingly
The read-only activation and its reserved names
requirements.gap: Direct bindings and _this are gated. _id and _now are specified but unimplemented in every SDK; _today is caller-supplied per spec but defaults to the host clock in Python and TypeScript. Tracked as implementation defects.

requirements.statement: ctx carries host-supplied data and never carries secrets or authorization decisions
requirements.gap: ctx is bound in .NET, Python and TypeScript but declared with a different element type in each, so a portable expression over ctx is not yet guaranteed. No corpus vector.

requirements.statement: exprValue marks provenance and never overwrites an unmarked non-empty response
Evaluation terminates and a reached bound applies the hint fallback
requirements.gap: Degradation on failure is gated. Exact bounds are implementation-defined in this baseline, so no vector asserts a limit.
